entry.gap: Most Table 2-4 parameters are assessed as 30-day rolling averages. VOL-II 7.2-7.3 do not say how such a parameter is 'met', or what counts as 'a failure', within the run: an average over the run, a daily rolling value using pre-run data, or individual samples. ADD-03 3.1-3.2 add an inlet flow range and say a day outside it 'shall not count towards the thirty (30) days'. They do not say whether such a day breaks the 'continuous' run, or whether a Table 2-4 failure on a non-counting day restarts it under 7.3.
entry.practical_impact: A failure restarts the full 30 days. PCOD timing drives delay liquidated damages of SAR 180,000 per day (VOL-V 18.1) and the 365-day termination right (VOL-V 18.3). Under ADD-03 Q17, the Independent Engineer's reasonable costs for any run after the first fall on the Project Company. The commissioning programme and float depend on the answer.
entry.proposed_question: Volume II, Clauses 7.2 and 7.3, page 4 (as amended by Addendum No. 3): (a) For Table 2-4 parameters whose basis of assessment is a 30-day rolling average, how is compliance determined during the 30-day reliability run? In particular, is the rolling average calculated over the run period only, or for each day of the run using data from before it began? What constitutes 'a failure' of such a parameter for the purposes of Clause 7.3? (b) Does a day on which the daily average flow is outside the range in Clause 7.2 interrupt the continuity of the run, or is it only excluded from the count of thirty (30) days? Does a Table 2-4 failure on such a day restart the run?
entry.interim_handling: Plan commissioning so that individual samples meet the rolling-average limits before the run starts. Plan inlet flow management to keep within 85-110% of nominal capacity. Hold programme float and Independent Engineer cost for at least one full restart, and record this as a programme assumption.
